title: Paper I  -  Foundational Claim

canonical_node.axiom: The foundational claim is the single bedrock assumption; if false, the entire paper fails.
definitions: Foundational Axiom: the one-sentence bedrock assumption of the paper.
F.A.C.T.S. Format: Find, Admit, Claim, Test, Snap.
Kill Condition: a specified threshold that, if met, falsifies the paper.
derivation: The paper is structured to state an axiom, then find an anomaly, admit bias, claim a thesis, test it, and define kill conditions.
The thesis is supported by three supporting arguments and makes predictions for true and false cases.
The test method includes tools, evidence table, primary finding, unexpected, and null results.
Kill conditions are explicitly invited to falsify the paper.
canonical_node.action: The system should treat this document as a template for a foundational claim paper, requiring the author to fill in each section with specific content, and to run the Lowe Battery tests.
boundary: This document is a template, not a completed paper; it contains no actual claims or evidence.
It does not assert any specific scientific or theological truth.
It does not provide a proof or derivation of any kind.
test: Check that each section (F, A, C, T, S) is filled with substantive content.
Verify that the foundational axiom is stated in one sentence.
Verify that kill conditions are defined with thresholds and status.
Verify that the Lowe Battery tests are answered with Pass/Fail.

dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a structured format for presenting a foundational claim, including explicit bias declaration and kill conditions.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the requirement for a single bedrock assumption and explicit falsification criteria.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If the foundational axiom section is removed, the paper loses its basis and cannot be evaluated.

classification.recommended_atom_action: Store as template; do not treat as a substantive claim.

overstatement_risks: Could be mistaken for a completed paper with actual findings.
The template's structure might imply a proof exists when it does not.
kill_conditions: If the template is presented as a completed paper without content.
If the foundational axiom is not stated or is ambiguous.

plain_summary: This is a template for a foundational claim paper, not a completed document. It outlines sections for axiom, find, admit, claim, test, and snap, but contains no actual content. It should be treated as a structural guide, not as a source of claims or evidence.
